checks: Repeated debug/release, compiled production mutant and restored hashes; see model.md#tests
cost: O(n) validation and O(log n) binary search, O(1) storage, no allocation. Caller budget bounds validated knots; overflow rejects rather than wrapping. Work budget is not a wall-clock deadline. No approximate floating evaluation or relative error tier is advertised.
description: At least two strictly increasing i64 abscissae with i64 ordinates and an integer in-domain query. Exact rational chord value N/h, where N=y_left*(x_right-x)+y_right*(x-x_left). Exact knot queries return ordinate/1. Under caller-supplied exact samples of a C² function on full domain with |f''|<=M, absolute error<=M*h²/8.
forward: At least two strictly increasing i64 abscissae with i64 ordinates and an integer in-domain query. Exact rational chord value N/h, where N=y_left*(x_right-x)+y_right*(x-x_left). Exact knot queries return ordinate/1. Under caller-supplied exact samples of a C² function on full domain with |f''|<=M, absolute error<=M*h²/8.
inverse: A rational output N/h constrains a weighted sum of neighboring ordinates. Infinitely many underlying C² functions have the same samples and midpoint while respecting sufficiently large curvature. Querying exact knot0,y0 admits different neighboring knots. Even with fixed samples, adding c*(x-a)*(x-b) changes interior values while preserving endpoint data.
limitations: Finite oracles do not establish universal accuracy
No performance measurement or automatic substitution
This kernel allocates no storage and has no allocation-error variant
